DataFrame.summary: pandas.DataFrame is a two-dimensional, size-mutable table with labeled rows and columns. It supports heterogeneous column types and label-aligned operations.
DataFrame.explanation: DataFrame constructs a two-dimensional table whose rows and columns have labels. It can hold columns with different data types, aligns arithmetic by both axes, and accepts common inputs such as dictionaries, arrays, Series, or another DataFrame.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Input data used to construct the table; the page supports values such as dictionaries, arrays, Series, and DataFrames.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Labels for the resulting rows; defaults to a generated RangeIndex when no index information is available.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: Labels for columns, or selection and ordering of existing labeled columns.

parameters.name: dtype
parameters.description: A single data type to force across the constructed DataFrame.

parameters.name: copy
parameters.description: Whether to copy input data; the default is context-dependent in the documented signature.

DataFrame.returns: A pandas DataFrame containing labeled rows and columns.

example.title: Create and select a DataFrame
example.code:
import pandas as pd

people = pd.DataFrame(
    {"name": ["Ada", "Linus"], "age": [36, 54]},
    index=["a", "l"],
)
people["adult"] = people["age"] >= 18
print(people.loc["a", ["name", "adult"]])
example.explanation: Creates a labeled DataFrame from column data, adds a derived column, and selects values by labels.

import pandas as pd

example.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"temp_c": [17.0, 25.0]})
result = df.assign(
    temp_f=lambda frame: frame["temp_c"] * 9 / 5 + 32,
    label=lambda frame: frame["temp_f"].round(0).astype(str) + "°F",
)

print(result)

import pandas as pd

pd.to_datetime.summary: Converts scalar, array-like, Series, or DataFrame-like values into pandas datetime objects. Options control parsing formats, errors, timezone handling, numeric units, origin, and caching.
pd.to_datetime.explanation: Pass a scalar, sequence, Series, or DataFrame-like value to parse it into pandas datetime objects. Control parsing errors, timezone localization, date ordering, units, origin, format matching, and caching with the optional arguments; the result type follows the input shape.
pd.to_datetime.syntax: pandas.to_datetime(arg, errors='raise', dayfirst=False, yearfirst=False, utc=False, format=None, exact=<no_default>, unit=None, origin='unix', cache=True)

parameters.name: arg
parameters.type: int, float, str, datetime, list, tuple, 1-d array, Series, DataFrame/dict-like
parameters.description: Value to convert: int, float, str, datetime, list, tuple, one-dimensional array, Series, or DataFrame/dict-like.

parameters.name: errors
parameters.description: Parsing error behavior: raise an exception, coerce invalid values to NaT, or ignore errors.

parameters.name: dayfirst
parameters.description: Prefer day-first interpretation for ambiguous dates.

parameters.name: yearfirst
parameters.description: Prefer year-first interpretation for ambiguous dates.

parameters.name: utc
parameters.description: Convert or localize results to UTC.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Parsing format, such as '%d/%m/%Y', or 'mixed' for per-element inference.

parameters.name: exact
parameters.description: Require the format to match exactly when not using a special format.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Unit for numeric values, such as 's', 'ms', 'us', or 'ns'.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Reference point for numeric timestamps; defaults to Unix epoch.

parameters.name: cache
parameters.description: Cache unique parsed date strings to improve repeated conversions.

pd.to_datetime.returns: Return type follows the input: scalar returns Timestamp (or datetime.datetime fallback); array-like returns DatetimeIndex (or object-dtype Series fallback); Series returns Series; DataFrame/dict-like returns a Series. example.title: Parse date strings
example.code:
import pandas as pd

values = pd.to_datetime(
    ["2024-01-15", "15/02/2024"],

)

Scalars return Timestamp-like values, array-like inputs return DatetimeIndex, and Series or DataFrame inputs preserve their corresponding structure.

utc=True converts timezone-aware inputs to UTC and localizes naive inputs to UTC.

pd.to_numeric.explanation: pandas.to_numeric parses a scalar or one-dimensional collection into numeric values. By default, invalid text raises an exception; choose coercion to produce missing values, and optionally request a smaller compatible dtype with downcast.

parameters.description: Value or one-dimensional collection to convert to numeric data.

parameters.name: errors
parameters.description: Controls invalid parsing: raise an exception or replace invalid values with NaN.

parameters.name: downcast

pd.to_numeric.returns: Numeric value or collection; return type depends on input, with Series input producing a Series and other supported inputs producing an ndarray.

pivot_table.summary: Creates a spreadsheet-style DataFrame by grouping input rows along index and column keys, then aggregating selected values. The output may use MultiIndex objects for its row and column axes.
pivot_table.explanation: Pass a DataFrame to pandas.pivot_table, choose grouping keys for the result index and columns, and specify the values and aggregation function. example.title: Summarize grouped values
example.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "region": ["East", "East", "West"],
    "product": ["A", "B", "A"],
    "sales": [10, 20, 15],
})

summary = pd.pivot_table(
    df,
    values="sales",
    index="region",
    columns="product",
    aggfunc="sum",
    fill_value=0,
)
print(summary)
example.explanation: Groups sales by region and product, sums each group, and replaces missing combinations with zero.

Series.summary: pandas.Series is a one-dimensional labeled data structure, including support for time-series data. It supports label- and integer-based indexing plus index-aware operations.
Series.explanation: Use Series for one-dimensional labeled data. Construct it from array-like data, a mapping, or a scalar, optionally supplying labels, a dtype, and a name; indexing and arithmetic use those labels.

import pandas as pd

scores = pd.Series([80, 95, 70], index=["ana", "bo", "cy"], name="score")
print(scores.loc["bo"])
print((scores + pd.Series({"ana": 5, "bo": 0, "cy": 10})).to_dict())

keyPoints: Series stores one-dimensional data together with an index, making it suitable for labeled columns or time-series values.
Values can be accessed using positional indexing or labels, depending on the indexing method used.
The constructor accepts sequence-like data, mappings, iterables, or a scalar.
When an index is supplied, its labels must be hashable and match the data length.
Omitting the index creates a default integer RangeIndex.
Binary operations combine the operand indexes into their sorted union.
gotchas: Labels may repeat, but every label must be hashable, so duplicate or unsuitable labels can affect selection behavior.
